posts.body:
Element of the day: Helium (He, 2).

Helium was detected in the Sun's spectrum in 1868, before it was confirmed on Earth. Its name comes from Helios, the Sun.

A little astronomy in the periodic table:
{url}
posts.fact_checked: Solar spectral discovery in 1868; terrestrial confirmation in 1895; Helios etymology.

posts.body:
Element of the day: Lithium (Li, 3).

A neutral lithium atom has three electrons: two in its first shell and one in its second. That outer electron is a useful clue to its Group 1 chemistry.

Explore Li:
{url}
posts.fact_checked: Group 1; Z=3; electron configuration [He] 2s1 implies shell occupancy 2,1.

Element of the day: Carbon (C, 6).

Diamond and graphite are both forms of pure carbon. Different atomic arrangements give them very different properties.

What else can the same element become?
{url}

posts.body:
Element of the day: Nitrogen (N, 7).

Nitrogen gas makes up about 78% of Earth's air by volume. Nitrogen compounds also help build the molecules of living things.

Explore the element around us:
{url}

posts.body:
Element of the day: Oxygen (O, 8).

Oxygen gas makes up about 21% of Earth's atmosphere by volume. Every oxygen atom has eight protons, whether it's in air, water or a rock.

Explore O on Elementa:
{url}
posts.fact_checked: Atmosphere about 21% oxygen by volume; atomic number 8 defines eight protons.

Element of the day: Neon (Ne, 10).

Element of the day: Sodium (Na, 11).

Element of the day: Silicon (Si, 14).

Silicon is a semiconductor. Tiny amounts of added elements can change its electrical properties, which helps make modern electronics possible.

Meet the element inside the chip:
{url}

Element of the day: Iron (Fe, 26).

Iron is part of haemoglobin, the protein that carries oxygen in your blood. Its chemistry matters in living cells as well as in steel.

Explore Fe on Elementa:
{url}
posts.fact_checked: Iron occurs in haemoglobin; haemoglobin transports oxygen; iron is the main constituent of steel.
